name: Apex 5" freestyle quad
note: The hero vehicle: ImpulseRC's 225 mm Apex 5 carbon frame (115 g), the T-Motor F60 Pro IV 1950 KV, the dataset's 4S racing pack and a RunCam Split HD camera. The propeller is APC's 5x4.5 bullnose, because it is the only 5-inch propeller with published coefficients, and those are APC's own computed figures, which run above measurements, so read the thrust as optimistic. The Gemfan 51466 most 5-inch builds fly has no published test data, so the app cannot model it. The F60 Pro IV V2.0 is a 6S motor; on 4S it spins slower and the 120C pack covers its current easily. The sprint mission's speed is not judged: ImpulseRC publishes no drag figure for the frame, so there is no top-speed estimate.
source: https://fpvua.com/en/motor-t-motor-f60-pro-iv-v2-0-2207-5-1950kv/ (T-Motor F60 Pro IV V2.0 1950KV: 33.4 g, 60 mΩ, 42 A, 949 W, 6S); frame: http://web.archive.org/web/20201108010422/http://apex.impulserc.com/ (Apex 5: 225 mm, 5.2" props, ~115 g)
about: A classic 5-inch freestyle FPV quad: a stiff carbon true-X frame, four fast-spinning motors and a camera tilted up for flying fast and low. This is the kind of drone pilots use for flips, dives and racing lines, flown through FPV goggles.

name: Apex 5" urban scan light
note: The lightest Apex build the dataset allows, aimed at the sub-250 g urban scan: BrotherHobby's VY 1504.5 3950 KV (12.07 g), the 80 g 3S pack, the 5-inch APC prop and the camera the mission requires. It cannot get under the mission's 249 g limit. The Apex frame alone is 115 g, and the build comes out near 314 g; a real sub-250 g build uses a smaller frame, which is what the CineLog25 preset does. The VY 1504.5 is a 3-inch motor (BrotherHobby tests it on a 3-inch tri-blade), so a 5-inch propeller holds it to its 13.2 A test maximum. The app flags that, and it also flags the endurance shortfall.
source: https://www.brotherhobbystore.com/products/vy-15045-motor-cw (BrotherHobby VY 1504.5 3950KV test report: 12.07 g, 139.74 mΩ, 13.20 A, 211.20 W, 3-inch propeller)
about: The same 5-inch frame stripped down with smaller motors and a lighter pack, as an attempt at a light urban inspection drone. It shows how hard it is to make a 5-inch build light enough for the strictest small-drone rules.

name: Apex 5" medical courier
note: The heavy-lift stretch: the 500 g cargo design mass under Tattu's real 4500 mAh 6S pack, on the 5-inch Apex with the F60 Pro IV. It lifts the load, but the app blocks it. Four F60s at full throttle on 6S want about 168 A, and the pack is rated 25C, 112.5 A. The earlier record's 45C pack, which would have covered that, does not exist. It is also short of the 15 km mission's 18 minutes. The cargo pod is a design mass, not a product (see the payload record). A real courier flies a winged VTOL, and the dataset's VTOL preset is the VTBIRD mapper.
about: A 5-inch quad asked to carry a small cargo pod under its frame, with a much bigger battery. It is a stretch build that shows what happens when a sport frame is pushed into delivery work.

name: Eclipson Model A thermal scout
note: The fixed wing: Eclipson's 1 m 3D-printed Model A in LW-PLA (220 g printed, 490 g take-off per Eclipson) with a Sunnysky X2216-III 880 KV on an APC 9x6E. Sunnysky's own table tests that motor on that prop. It carries the 80 g 3S pack, inside Eclipson's "2S or 3S, 500 mAh to 1500 mAh", and the thermal core the search-and-rescue mission requires. Eclipson proposes a lighter Sunnysky X2212 1250 KV on an 8x6, which the dataset does not carry, so this pairing is heavier than Eclipson's. Eclipson publishes a stall speed (24 km/h at 490 g) but no drag figure. So the app checks speed at 1.4 times the stall speed, which falls short of the mission's 10 m/s, and it does not judge cruise endurance.
source: https://www.eclipson-airplanes.com/modela (Eclipson Model A: 1000 mm span, 16 dm², 220 g printed LW-PLA, 490 g take-off, stall 24 km/h, 2S-3S 500-1500 mAh)
about: A small 3D-printed fixed-wing plane carrying a thermal camera core. A wing flies on lift rather than motor thrust, so it can stay up far more efficiently than a quad, which is why search-and-rescue teams like planes for covering ground.

name: CineLog25 urban cinewhoop
note: The build the urban-light preset could not be: GEPRC's 114 mm ducted CineLog25 V2 frame (70.9 g), the 4500 KV 1404 motor GEPRC fits it, a 63 mm ducted three-blade propeller and the 660 mAh 4S HV pack GEPRC recommends, plus the camera the mission requires. It comes in near 232 g, under the 249 g line, and lifts more than five times its weight. What it cannot do is stay up: a 10 Wh pack gives a few minutes of real flying, which is what GEPRC itself quotes (4 to 6 minutes), so the app will flag the mission's 14-minute endurance. Two honest caveats: the stock propeller is a four-blade HQ DT63 with no published test data, so this uses the three-blade Gemfan D63 that has one, and on that propeller the motor reaches its 13.38 A rating at full throttle, which the app also flags. The duct is drawn but not modelled: no source measures its effect.
about: A 2.5-inch cinewhoop: a tiny quad with a duct around every propeller so it can fly close to people and buildings and bump into things safely. Cinewhoops are made for smooth indoor and close-up video.

name: Chimera7 Pro long-range
note: The long-range quad: iFlight's 327 mm Chimera7 Pro V2 with its stock XING2 2809 1250 KV motors and the 8000 mAh 6S Li-ion pack iFlight quotes its 30-minute hover on. The O4 air unit, GPS and flight stack ride in the frame's electronics weight, so no separate camera is fitted. It comes out near 1.56 kg (iFlight publishes about 1.62 kg with this pack) and a hover just over half an hour, in line with iFlight's own claim; the mixed figure is what the ridge run is judged on. The propeller is a 7-inch Gemfan 7040 tri-blade rather than the stock HQ 7.5-inch, because iFlight's motor test only covers the 7040; its coefficients are worked back from that one full-throttle test point, so treat the thrust as an estimate. There is no top-speed estimate: iFlight publishes 140 km/h, but the frame record has no drag data to check it with.
source: https://shop.iflight.com/Chimera7-Pro-V2-6S-O4-HD-Pro2259 (iFlight Chimera7 Pro V2 6S O4 HD: "Takeoff Weight incl. 8000mAH: Approx. 1621±5g", "Max Hover Time: Approx. 30 min (No load With 21700 6S 8000mAH)")
about: A 7-inch long-range FPV quad with a large Li-ion pack, built for long, efficient cruising out to a distant point and back. The bigger, slower propellers trade punch for endurance.

name: Tarot X6 multispectral mapper
note: The heavy lifter: Tarot's 960 mm folding hexacopter on six T-Motor MN4014 330 KV motors with the 17x5.8 carbon propeller T-Motor recommends for them, a 16 Ah 6S Tattu Plus pack and a MicaSense RedEdge-P multispectral camera. Six ESCs are counted in the electronics weight, which brings it to about 6 kg. It lifts about three times its weight and hovers a little over 20 minutes, but mixed flying takes it just under the survey's 15-minute target, and the app will say so. It also flags the motors at their 25 A rating on full throttle. T-Motor's own table tops out at 17 A and 2.6 kg a motor; this app's simple motor model asks for more at full voltage, so read the thrust as an upper bound. Tarot publishes no flight time for this combination, so there is no published figure to check against.
source: https://store.tmotor.com/product/mn4014-kv330-motor-navigator-type.html (T-Motor MN4014 KV330: recommended prop "T-MOTOR P17*5.8"; 22.2 V test, 50 % throttle 1050 g at 104.34 W, 100 % 2600 g at 377.40 W)
about: A large folding hexacopter carrying a multispectral survey camera. Six motors give it spare lift and keep it steady while it flies grid patterns over fields to map crop health.

name: VTBIRD VTOL multispectral mapper
note: The winged VTOL: XUWING's 1.6 m EPO VTBIRD in its 4+1 quadplane form, the mapping and survey aircraft it is sold as, with Sunnysky X4112S lift motors on 13x5 EOLO props, the Sunnysky X3520-III pusher Finwing's power combo names, a single 6S 16 Ah pack (inside Finwing's recommended 16-22 Ah) and the MicaSense multispectral camera, which sits inside the kit's 0.4-0.8 kg payload range. It comes out near 5.4 kg, inside Finwing's 4.5-5.5 kg 4+1 range, and lifts a little over twice its weight on the four lift rotors. Three honest substitutions: Finwing's lift motor is an X4112S 485KV with no published numbers, so Sunnysky's published KV450 winding stands in; its pusher prop is a 14x8, but Sunnysky only publishes test data for the APC 14x7; and the airframe weight is Finwing's flight-test aircraft (5.3 kg less its 2.3 kg battery), not a part-by-part sum. Finwing publishes no drag figure, so cruise endurance and range are not judged: the app works out hover on the lift rotors and checks speed against Finwing's measured 19 m/s cruise. Finwing's own test flew 1 h 44 min and 95 km.
source: https://www.finwinghobby.com/goods.php?id=166 (XUWING VTBIRD 4+1 kit + power combo: 1600 mm span, 40 dm², kit 1.05 kg, 4+1 AUW 4.5-5.5 kg, 4 x X4112S KV485 lift, Sunnysky X3520 III KV560 pusher, battery "6S 16000-22000mah"; flight-test sheet: "Plane AUW 5.3kg" with 2.3 kg of battery, cruise 19 m/s)
about: A VTOL quadplane: it takes off and lands straight up on four lift rotors, then flies like a plane on its wing with a rear pusher propeller. That mix lets a survey drone launch without a runway and still cover a lot of ground.
